Garden water

Deep Forensic All Paths Taken Multi-Vendor Investigation

This proposed charter asks how independent reviewers would count the same 36 descriptions. The garden example contains no submitted vendor reports or approval decisions.

Proposed charter

The Architect supplies the domain and scope, decides the three approval gates below and would relay each vendor’s output verbatim. The Lead Investigator would design the charter, allocate work, issue complete task packets and coordinate the investigation between gates.

A source reviewer would compare the two numbered lists and record each addition. A route reviewer would trace branches, returns and shared destinations. A separate divergence reviewer would receive only the frozen evidence and their own task packet. The other reviewers’ findings would be withheld from that reviewer.

Task packet for the independent divergence reviewer

Investigation identifier
Garden water study one, independent counting review.
Domain and scope
Possible water transfers in the garden example. Use only the two supplied lists and their numbered entries.
Central question
Which additions open new transfers, connect existing transfers, or describe an existing transfer more closely?
Temporal and geographic parameters
Compare the first 16 entries with the expanded list of 36. Both concern an illustrative garden and its named surroundings. The time of each physical transfer and the site coordinates are unknown.
Entities
Puddle, soil, stream, groundwater, plant, fruit, bird, snail, atmosphere, neighboring roof, gutter, barrel and hose.
Task
Count immediate puddle exits in each snapshot. Trace a route back to a bird. Compare plant-to-fruit with stem-to-fruit. Mark any join that would require an unlisted transfer.
Output format
Return a numbered list of findings. For each, give the entry numbers, counting rule, assumptions, alternatives and missing observation. Preserve unresolved differences as separate rows.

What independent divergence could reveal

One reviewer might count all 36 descriptions. Another might count distinct transfers and flag the possible overlap between entry 12 and entry 19. Those answers use different units. A second test asks whether a return to a bird establishes the identity of the individual bird. A third asks whether water inside a leaf can join a route starting on its surface. The Lead Investigator would compare the stated assumptions and retain each original answer beside its source references.

Approval gates

  1. Charter · proposed, awaiting decision. The Architect would review scope, source lists, allocation, packets, paths and deliverables.
  2. Evidence Freeze · pending. The Lead Investigator would present the classified register, verbatim extracts, source bindings, claim qualifications and evidence-strength assessments. The Architect would decide whether to lock that record for formal analysis.
  3. Final Package · pending. The Lead Investigator would assemble the evidence register, independent reports, cross-path findings and unresolved differences. The Architect would decide whether to approve the package or request changes.

Separate analysis freeze

The analysis register remains open. A formal freeze requires the Architect’s explicit direction to “freeze analysis register.” The three review gates above each cover a different decision.
